title: Fifteen-Two
teaser: The old pub card game with a peg board, finally easy to follow. Play to 31, throw two cards to the crib, and watch every fifteen, pair and run light up as your pegs leap down the board. Count it yourself the 1980 way, or let the cards count for you.

manPage.synopsis: fifteen-two — cribbage with a peg board: lay away to the crib, play to 31, and watch every fifteen, pair and run light up.
manPage.description: Earl T. Cohen wrote the game logic and Ken Arnold the screen interface for the Berkeley cribbage in 1980. It never counted your hand for you: claim too much and the computer pegged two, claim too little and the rest was lost, and a claim of 19 meant nothing at all. Fifteen-Two keeps that way of counting as Classic 1980, plays Cohen’s own computer player card for card, and adds a wooden board, a sharper opponent, a counting trainer and a Daily Discard.

howToPlay: Keep four of your six cards and lay two away in the crib, which belongs to the dealer.
Take turns laying cards towards 31, pegging for fifteens, pairs, runs, 31 and the last card.
Count your hand with the starter, then the crib, and be first round the board.
